title: Test Suite Architecture
concept: The XIOM compiler test suite — thousands of tests ensuring every compiler feature works correctly, from parsing to code generation.
why: A compiler without a test suite is a bug generator. The XIOM test suite contains tens of thousands of tests — each one preventing a regression.
theory:
## Testing the Compiler

### Test Categories

| Category | Count | Description |
|----------|-------|-------------|
| Unit tests | 5000+ | Test individual compiler functions |
| Parse tests | 2000+ | Test lexer/parser with valid and invalid input |
| Type tests | 3000+ | Test type checker with valid and invalid types |
| Borrow tests | 2000+ | Test borrow checker rules |
| Codegen tests | 1500+ | Verify generated LLVM IR |
| Runtime tests | 1000+ | Compile and run programs, check output |
| Regression tests | 3000+ | Tests for fixed bugs (never break again) |
| Contract tests | 500+ | Test contract verification |

### Test Structure

```
tests/
├── unit/              # Unit tests for compiler internals
│   ├── lexer/
│   ├── parser/
│   └── checker/
├── parse/             # Parse → check AST
├── typeck/            # Type check → check errors
├── borrowck/          # Borrow check → check errors
├── codegen/           # Compile → check IR output
├── run-pass/          # Compile + run → expect exit 0
├── run-fail/          # Compile + run → expect exit != 0
├── compile-fail/      # Compile should fail with specific error
└── fixed/             # Regression tests for fixed bugs
```

### Expect Tests

```xiom
// compile-fail/E101_type_mismatch.xi
fn main() -> Int {
  let x: Int = "hello";  //~ ERROR: type mismatch
  return 0;
}
```

The `//~ ERROR:` comment specifies what error is expected. The test framework compiles the file, captures errors, and verifies they match the annotations.

### Snapshot Testing

```
// run-pass/hello_world.xi
fn main() -> Int {
  io.println("Hello, XIOM!");
  return 0;
}

// hello_world.stdout (expected output):
Hello, XIOM!
```

### Running the Test Suite

```sh
# Run all tests
xiom test --compiler

# Run specific category
xiom test --compiler --tests parse

# Run tests matching pattern
xiom test --compiler --filter "borrow"

# Update snapshots
xiom test --compiler --bless
```
syntax_ref:
# Run compiler tests:
xiom test --compiler
xiom test --compiler --filter "type_mismatch"

# Update test expectations:
xiom test --compiler --bless

# Test file annotation:
//~ ERROR: type mismatch    (expect this error)
//~| HELP: consider using    (continuation of diagnostic)
tips: Write regression tests for EVERY bug you fix — prevent it from returning
Expect tests are self-documenting — they show what error should occur and why
The test suite is the specification — if tests pass, the compiler is correct
Run the full suite before submitting PRs — partial test runs miss regressions
common_mistakes: Writing tests that pass for the wrong reason — ensure the test FAILS before your fix
Not updating tests when changing compiler behavior — use --bless to update snapshots
Focusing only on happy-path tests — negative tests (compile-fail) are equally important
